If you activate before attacking with a Digimon, [EX12-074 Genshi Continent & Ashino Island]'s {Security} [Your Turn] effect becomes a derived triggering effect, allowing the Digimon to digivolve into the specified card. After all processing that results from digivolving is resolved, and before the counter timing, you can activate this card's [End of Your Turn] effect that is pending activation.

qa.answer:
You place the top card of one of your Digimon in the digivolution cards of that Digimon or another of your Digimon.
This doesn't include when the top card becomes a digivolution card through digivolution.
qa.question: What does "when an effect places the top card of one of your Digimon in a Digimon's digivolution cards" in this card's [Your Turn] effect mean, exactly?

qa.answer:
No, it doesn’t.
The [On Play] effect will trigger, but it can't activate because the Digimon becomes a digivolution card through DNA digivolution before the effect activates.

qa.answer:
Yes, it can be blocked.
is an effect that allows for the Digimon to block, so it isn't affected by ""isn't affected by the effects of your opponent's Digimon"" effects.
qa.question: If this Digimon attacks when this card's [On Play][When Attacking] effect prevents it from being affected by the effects of my opponent's Digimon, can it be blocked by my opponent's Digimon?

qa.answer:
No. The effect reads ""You may choose,"" so you don't have to choose a Digimon.
In such cases, the attack doesn't occur.
qa.question: Do I have to choose an opponent's Digimon and have my opponent attack for this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect?

qa.answer: No, you don't have to choose an opponent's Digimon.
qa.question: Do I have to choose an opponent's Digimon for this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect?

qa.answer: No, they can't attack using a Digimon that can't attack.
qa.question: If I choose an opponent's Digimon that can't attack for this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect, does my opponent attack with that Digimon?

qa.answer:
No, your opponent can't attack using that Digimon. A new attack declaration can't be made during an attack.
In such cases, even if you choose an opponent's Digimon for this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect when there is already an attacking Digimon, your opponent can't attack with the chosen Digimon.
qa.question:
An opponent's Digimon is attacking using an effect at the end of their turn.
If I choose an opponent's Digimon for this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect, does my opponent attack with that Digimon?

qa.answer:
Yes, you can choose a Digimon that isn't affected by effects for this and have it attack.
Such Digimon aren't affected by effects, but they can be chosen.
In addition, "your opponent attacks with the chosen Digimon" in this card's [End of Opponent’s Turn] effect affects a player, therefore your opponent must attack with the chosen Digimon if it can attack.
